finalText:
Found it. The pricing engine was rounding intermediate values in USD after each discount, then converting currencies, then rounding again. This caused precision loss.

When you apply a 10% discount to $19.98, you get $17.982. Rounding that to $17.98 and then converting to GBP at 0.78 gives 14.0244 → 14.02. But if you skip the intermediate rounding and convert first (17.982 × 0.78 = 14.0259...), then round, you get 14.03—the correct answer.

The test reference implementation only rounds once, at the very end in the target currency. I removed the intermediate `round()` calls after applying percent and flat discounts. All 40 tests pass now.
